item.statement: det(I+tH)=(1+t)^nu via triangularity, Sylvester/principal-minor expansion, Hadamard bound on Gram determinants, then Bernstein integral x^r = (r sin pi r/pi) int log(1+xt) t^{-1-r} dt to pass to power sums
item.what_to_check: Cite Horn-Johnson for Sylvester/Hadamard; check majorization literature (Bhatia; Marshall-Olkin) for the generating-function-to-power-sum transfer

chk.evidence:
Every step of the technique in app:cost is standard. The inequality it proves, sum_l|beta_l|^r >= nu^{1-r}|beta|^r for 0<r<=1, also has a two-line classical proof.

(a) Sylvester's determinant identity, the principal-minor expansion of det(I+tX), and Hadamard's inequality for Gram/PSD matrices are textbook results in Horn & Johnson, Matrix Analysis, 2nd ed. I confirmed the book on cambridge.org. I did not verify section numbers.

(b) The integral x^r = (r sin(pi r)/pi) ∫ log(1+xt) t^{-1-r} dt is the Stieltjes/complete-Bernstein representation of x^r. The operator-monotone chapter of Bhatia gives x^r = (sin r pi/pi) ∫ x/(x+lambda) lambda^{r-1} dlambda, and integrating by parts gives the log form. I did not verify Bhatia's section or equation numbers. I could not fetch the de Gruyter page for the Schilling-Song-Vondracek monograph.

(c) The step from the generating function to power sums (prod(1+x_l t) >= (1+t)^nu for all t implies sum x^r >= nu) has no named majorization-literature precedent that I found. It is not ordinary weak majorization, but it is elementary.

(d) Main finding: the lemma follows from two classical theorems.
- Weyl's majorant theorem: Weyl, PNAS 35:408-411, 1949, fetched via PMC; also Bhatia Thm II.3.6 per secondary sources. It says sum phi(|lambda_i|) <= sum phi(sigma_i) when phi(e^s) is convex. H is upper triangular with unit diagonal, so all its eigenvalues are 1, and with phi = x^r this gives nu <= sum sigma_i(H)^r.
- The Rotfel'd/Thompson inequality: R.C. Thompson, Pacific J. Math 66(1):285-290, 1976. I fetched the PDF. Its eq. (1) reads: "f(γ1)+...+f(γn) <= f(α1)+...+f(αn)+f(β1)+...+f(βn) when f is an increasing concave function of a nonnegative real variable, with f(0)=0", where α, β, γ are the singular values of A, B, A+B. Apply it to the rank-one summands d_l u_l u_l^* with f = x^r. This gives sum sigma_i(H)^r <= sum_l |d_l|^r.
- Together these give sum|d_l|^r >= nu, which is the lemma.

The paper's own route is still valuable because it gives the equality case cleanly. Searches run: Thompson 1976 title; Rotfel'd concave singular values; Weyl majorant Bhatia II.3.6; Weyl 1949 PNAS; Bernstein integral representation of x^r; Schilling-Song-Vondracek. Notes are in /Users/ruhaanrajadhyaksha/projects/grok/heracles/paper/litcheck/items/t3-determinant-gram/CHECK.md.

recommended_citations.why: Standard reference for the three facts used in Lemma minor and Lemma hadamard: Sylvester's identity det(I+UΔU*) = det(I+ΔU*U), the principal-minor expansion of det(I+tX), and Hadamard's inequality (Gram determinant <= product of diagonal entries, with equality iff the matrix is diagonal). Section numbers not verified.

Eq. (1), due to Rotfel'd: for increasing concave f with f(0)=0, sum f(sigma(A+B)) <= sum f(sigma(A)) + sum f(sigma(B)). With f = x^r and the rank-one summands d_l u_l u_l^*, this gives sum sigma_i(H)^r <= sum|d_l|^r, which is half of an alternative proof of Lemma cost.

Weyl's majorant theorem: sum phi(|lambda_i|) <= sum phi(sigma_i) for phi with phi(e^s) convex. Since H is triangular with unit eigenvalues, this gives nu <= sum sigma_i(H)^r. Combined with Thompson/Rotfel'd it yields the inequality of Lemma cost.

Textbook source for Weyl's majorant theorem (Thm II.3.6, per secondary sources) and for the integral representation of x^r (0<r<1) in the operator-monotone chapter (Ch. V). The log-kernel form in Lemma bernstein follows from that representation by integration by parts. Title, author and series were confirmed; the year 1997 comes from search metadata; theorem and equation numbers were not verified.

chk.recommended_change: In app:cost, cite Horn-Johnson [hornjohnson2012] at "Sylvester's identity", "Expanding by principal minors" and in Lemma hadamard ("Hadamard's inequality"). In Lemma bernstein, add "(the classical Stieltjes/complete-Bernstein representation of x^r; cf. [bhatia1997, Ch. V])". After the proof of Lemma cost, add one sentence: "The inequality (though not the equality case as we use it) also follows from Weyl's majorant theorem [weyl1949], which gives nu = sum|lambda_i(H)|^r <= sum sigma_i(H)^r, combined with the Rotfel'd-Thompson concave subadditivity of singular values [thompson1976], which gives sum sigma_i(H)^r <= sum_l |d_l|^r." Do not present the determinant/Gram technique as new.
